question: Should `openclaw/plugin-sdk/reply-payload` permanently expose the generic `tool-progress` constant and predicate for plugin producers and channel consumers?
rationale: The branch intentionally expands a public plugin contract; functional review can validate its implementation but cannot choose the long-term external API commitment.

options.title: Accept generic progress intent
options.body: Keep the additive API, document that it marks transient automatic tool summaries only, and require bundled consumers to gate it before representation-specific delivery.

options.title: Keep progress intent internal
options.body: Rework the branch to use an existing non-public boundary so third-party plugins do not gain a new permanent reply-payload contract.

recommendation.title: Accept generic progress intent
recommendation.body: Keep the additive API, document that it marks transient automatic tool summaries only, and require bundled consumers to gate it before representation-specific delivery.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged history spans both the structured Slack delivery path and the narrowed public reply-payload SDK surface.
